items.copy: An AI assistant can pass a website scan and still block a member at authentication, error recovery or the handoff to a person. Before launch, member-service leaders should test complete high-value tasks with assistive technology, preserve an equivalent human route and make any failed urgent or dispute scenario a release blocker. https://creditunionainews.com/insight-credit-union-ai-accessibility-test-plan.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-credit-union-ai-accessibility-test-plan-2026-08-20
items.imageAlt: Multiple accessible service routes converge through a control check before reaching a staffed member-service desk

items.copy: Treasury’s new GENIUS Act proposal asks whether a digital asset redeemable only in credit-union shares should count as a payment stablecoin. That question can move a tokenized-share or vendor plan into a licensing and control perimeter. Payments leaders should map the issuer, redemption promise, custody, marketing and monitoring roles before approving a pilot. https://creditunionainews.com/news/treasury-stablecoin-rule-credit-union-shares.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-treasury-stablecoin-rule-credit-union-shares-2026-08-19
items.imageAlt: A mixed-media token reaches a fork between a licensing gate and a cooperative member-share motif beside a regulatory ledger

items.copy: H.R. 10082 would open two new investment paths for federal credit unions—but it is only an introduced bill. Treasury leaders should use the signal now to map issuer limits, independent credit analysis, stress tests and board reporting, without changing portfolios before enactment and NCUA rulemaking. https://creditunionainews.com/news/federal-credit-union-investment-authority-bill.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-federal-credit-union-investment-authority-bill-2026-08-18
items.imageAlt: An ink illustration of a chained investment gate between bond certificates and structured security blocks, with a balance and control checklist in front

items.copy: Colorado’s ASSET Act is now in effect, requiring qualified credit-union employees to report suspected exploitation and creating an optional disbursement-delay path. Fraud and compliance leaders should test who starts a hold, who sends the two-day notices and how the 90-day decision clock is documented. https://creditunionainews.com/news/colorado-asset-act-credit-union-fraud-holds.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-colorado-asset-act-credit-union-fraud-holds-2026-08-17
items.imageAlt: A brass timing gate routes transaction tokens toward an evidence file, notification envelope and review tray

items.copy: FinCEN has permanently ended CTA beneficial-ownership reporting for U.S. companies—but credit unions' separate CDD duties remain. Compliance leaders should audit business-account scripts, knowledge bases and automated rules now so the reporting change does not accidentally switch off owner identification and verification. https://creditunionainews.com/news/fincen-boi-rule-credit-union-cdd.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-fincen-boi-rule-credit-union-cdd-2026-08-14
items.imageAlt: Ownership data splitting between a disappearing reporting path and a continuing identity-verification path into a secure vault

items.copy: Changing AI vendors is a continuity test, not a cancellation task. Credit-union leaders should require seven things before signing: dependency mapping, portable data and decision evidence, transition rights, a workable fallback, replacement validation, access shutdown and proof of data disposition. https://creditunionainews.com/insight-credit-union-ai-vendor-exit-playbook.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-credit-union-ai-vendor-exit-playbook-2026-08-13
items.imageAlt: Two modular AI platforms connected by a controlled bridge carrying data, model and audit components

items.copy: Breach response is not one deadline. Credit-union cyber teams should maintain three synchronized records: a containment-and-evidence log, a timestamped NCUA reportability decision, and a member-notification plan with named support owners. Guardian Credit Union's notice shows why waiting for a final forensic report can blur those separate clocks. https://creditunionainews.com/news/guardian-credit-union-data-breach-response.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-guardian-credit-union-data-breach-response-2026-08-11
items.imageAlt: Three analog clocks beside secured evidence, response controls and a sealed member-notification envelope

items.copy: Fraud teams should not treat a successful password or one-time code as the whole answer on authorization. The operating takeaway: reconstruct who created the payee, entered the amount and initiated the transfer—and preserve device, session and challenge evidence before deciding a Regulation E claim. https://creditunionainews.com/news/rbfcu-impersonation-scam-regulation-e-investigations.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-rbfcu-impersonation-scam-regulation-e-investigations-2026-08-10
items.imageAlt: Two spoofed call-signal paths separating through layered transaction-evidence controls

items.copy: Arizona Financial is sequencing its agentic AI program sensibly: unify member-service workflows first, automate later. The operational takeaway is to baseline handoff time, rework and exceptions before assigning agents any authority—and tier each task as suggest, prepare, limited execution or never automate. https://creditunionainews.com/news/arizona-financial-creatio-agentic-ai-workflows.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-arizona-financial-creatio-agentic-ai-workflows-2026-07-31
items.imageAlt: Editorial illustration of fragmented credit-union service workflows converging around a shared member profile

items.copy: Velera's new Risk Alert Manager shifts the fraud question from detection speed to response speed. For credit-union leaders, the operating takeaway is to measure alert-to-review, alert-to-action and member-resolution time separately—then balance faster card controls against false positives, unnecessary reissues and member friction. https://creditunionainews.com/news/velera-risk-alert-manager-fraud-response.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-velera-risk-alert-manager-fraud-response-2026-07-30
items.imageAlt: Linocut illustration of a fraud analyst directing suspicious card signals through response controls

items.copy: The Fed's proposed Payment Account could give more eligible institutions a streamlined route to FedNow and other payment services. Credit unions are asking the right operating question: who supervises the BSA/AML controls behind that access? The takeaway for executives is to map every partner's control perimeter—customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, incident response and regulator—before relying on a new direct-access payment provider. https://creditunionainews.com/news/credit-unions-fed-payment-account-guardrails.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-credit-unions-fed-payment-account-guardrails-2026-07-28

FinCEN's new student-aid fraud alert is an implementation brief for credit unions, not just a warning. The strongest detection pattern combines refund descriptors with beneficiary mismatch, new-account age, shared devices or IPs, and rapid movement through P2P, wires or digital assets. The operational takeaway: test whether your synthetic-identity and mule controls can see the one-refund/one-account model without treating one unusual transaction as determinative. https://creditunionainews.com/news/fincen-ai-student-aid-fraud.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-fincen-ai-student-aid-fraud-2026-07-27

Agentic AI is moving from alert scoring into the AML investigation itself. For credit-union compliance leaders, the operating test is whether every recommendation can be reconstructed: source data, investigative steps, escalation logic, analyst override and final decision. Start narrowly, sample cleared alerts as well as escalations, and keep regulated action behind human approval. https://creditunionainews.com/news/genpact-agentic-ai-aml-investigations.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-genpact-agentic-ai-aml-investigations-2026-07-24

Communication Federal Credit Union has moved AI credit decisioning from selection into production. The operational takeaway for lending leaders is to separate vendor forecasts from realized results and start measuring approval and pricing outcomes, adverse-action reasons, overrides, early delinquency and model drift at go-live. https://creditunionainews.com/news/communication-fcu-scienaptic-ai-lending.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=cuai_news&utm_content=linkedin-communication-fcu-scienaptic-ai-lending-2026-07-23

The most useful detail in Bank of America’s EricaAssist upgrade is not the model. It is the placement: AI assembles guidance inside the service employee’s workflow while the employee remains responsible for the conversation. For credit-union contact centers, that suggests a practical sequence—start with approved-source retrieval and next-step prompts, measure accuracy and repeat contacts alongside speed, and keep account changes behind existing approvals. What evidence would your team require before putting real-time AI guidance beside frontline staff? https://creditunionainews.com/news/bank-of-america-ericaassist-generative-ai.html
